blocks.name: Cat Age Calculator: Human Years & Stage

mainEntity.name: How old is a 1-year-old cat in human years?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 15 human years. Cats mature rapidly: a six-month-old kitten is roughly comparable to a 10-year-old child, and a two-year-old cat to a person in their mid-20s.
Veterinary education charts use 15 human years for the first year, 9 for the second, and about 4 for each year after that. It is an approximation for communication, not a biological law.

mainEntity.name: What are the feline life stages?

acceptedAnswer.text: The AAFP/AAHA Feline Life Stage Guidelines define kitten (birth to 1 year), young adult (1–6), mature adult (7–10), senior (11–14 in this tool), and geriatric (15+). Exact labels vary slightly between sources.

mainEntity.name: When should my cat start senior health screening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many veterinarians recommend exams at least twice a year from around age 10, with bloodwork, blood pressure, and weight monitoring. Cats hide illness well, so regular checks catch kidney disease, hyperthyroidism, and dental disease early.

mainEntity.name: Do indoor cats live longer than outdoor cats?

acceptedAnswer.text: On average, yes. Indoor cats avoid traffic, fights, and many infectious diseases, and often live well into their mid-to-late teens. The calculator does not adjust for lifestyle; it only maps age to life stage.

mainEntity.name: How can I tell my cat’s age if it is a rescue?

acceptedAnswer.text: A vet can estimate age from teeth, eyes, coat, and joint condition. Estimates are more reliable for kittens and young adults than for older cats.
